landing.hero.subheadline: Auth, payments, subscriptions, credits, RBAC, CMS, and i18n — all pre-wired. Just build your product on top.

landing.features.description: Pre-wired business logic so you can focus on building your product.
landing.features.auth.title: Authentication
landing.features.auth.description: Email/password, Google, and GitHub OAuth — ready out of the box with session management and account linking.
landing.features.payment.title: Payments
landing.features.payment.description: Stripe, PayPal, Alipay, WeChat Pay — checkout, subscriptions, webhooks, and order management.
landing.features.rbac.title: Roles & Permissions
landing.features.rbac.description: Fine-grained RBAC with wildcard matching. Full admin panel for managing users, roles, and permissions.
landing.features.i18n.title: Internationalization
landing.features.i18n.description: English and Chinese built-in with locale-aware routing. Easy to extend with additional languages.
landing.features.cms.title: Content Management
landing.features.cms.description: Categories and posts with full CRUD, status management, and admin panel — build your blog or docs.
landing.features.credits.title: Credit System
landing.features.credits.description: FIFO consumption, expiration, auto-grant on signup, and revocation — ready for usage-based billing.

landing.pricing.description: Choose the plan that works for you.
landing.faq.title: Frequently asked questions
landing.faq.description: Everything you need to know before getting started.
landing.faq.stack.question: What's the tech stack?
landing.faq.stack.answer: Next.js 16 with the App Router, React 19, TypeScript strict mode, Tailwind CSS 4, shadcn/ui, Drizzle ORM, and better-auth. Every piece of business logic is inlined — no external packages for payment, email, storage, or AI.
landing.faq.payment.question: Which payment providers are supported?
landing.faq.payment.answer: Stripe, PayPal, Creem, Alipay, and WeChat Pay out of the box. The PaymentManager abstraction makes it straightforward to add more providers by implementing a single interface.
landing.faq.database.question: Which databases can I use?
landing.faq.database.answer: Drizzle ORM handles PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, Turso, and Cloudflare D1. Switch providers by editing DATABASE_PROVIDER in your .env — the schema templates and drizzle config adapt automatically.
landing.faq.customize.question: How customizable is the landing page?
landing.faq.customize.answer: The src/blocks/ directory ships with demo sections — they're designed to be rewritten per project. The durable primitives live in src/components/, so your rebrand touches blocks and translations, not the chassis.
landing.faq.license.question: Can I use this for commercial projects?
landing.faq.license.answer: Yes. ShipAny Next is built for shipping production SaaS products. You own the code after cloning — no per-seat fees, no runtime dependencies on our infrastructure.
landing.cta.headline: Ready to ship your SaaS?
landing.cta.subheadline: Stop wiring auth, payments, and RBAC from scratch. Start with ShipAny Next and build what actually makes your product unique.

game.leaderboard.page_description: See the best simulated win percentages against the 2015-16 Warriors on 73-9.org. Today, this week, and all-time boards — sign in to save your runs.
game.leaderboard.seo.title: What the 73-9 leaderboard tracks
game.leaderboard.seo.intro: Every entry on this board is a starting five that took on the 2015-16 Golden State Warriors in an 82-game simulation at 73-9.org. Rankings sort by win percentage against that historic club — the same number you see when a run finishes.
game.leaderboard.seo.rank.heading: How rankings are decided
game.leaderboard.seo.rank.p1: After you lock five contracts under the $100M bankroll, the game simulates a full season and reports how often your five beats the 2015-16 Warriors. That win percentage is the score that lands here. Higher is better; ties break toward newer results.
game.leaderboard.seo.rank.p2: The board shows the account name, win %, and the simulated W–L line for each listed run. It is a public snapshot of the strongest submissions — not a prediction of real NBA outcomes, and not affiliated with the league or any team.
game.leaderboard.seo.windows.heading: Today, this week, and all-time
game.leaderboard.seo.windows.p1: Three windows sit side by side. Today covers runs since midnight UTC. This week covers Monday 00:00 UTC through now. All-time keeps the highest scores ever recorded on 73-9.org.
game.leaderboard.seo.windows.p2: A great night can push you to the top of Today without rewriting All-time. Climbing the long board means repeating strong bankroll decisions across many wheel draws — the same puzzle that makes the game hard.
game.leaderboard.seo.save.heading: Play free; sign in to appear
game.leaderboard.seo.save.p1: Anyone can play without an account. Guests still see the public boards and can finish a full run. Signed-in players automatically save each completed season so the result can rank here under their display name.
game.leaderboard.seo.save.p2: If you are not signed in, the results screen reminds you that the run will not be saved. Create an account or sign in from the header, play again, and your next finish posts to the leaderboard when it clears the top of a window.
game.leaderboard.seo.faq.title: Leaderboard FAQ
game.leaderboard.seo.faq.q1: What does win % mean on this board?
game.leaderboard.seo.faq.a1: It is how often your simulated five beats the 2015-16 Warriors over an 82-game season projection — the same percentage shown on the results screen after you play.
game.leaderboard.seo.faq.q2: Do I need an account to show up?
game.leaderboard.seo.faq.a2: Yes for ranking. Guests can play and browse the boards freely, but only signed-in runs are saved and eligible to appear under a name.
game.leaderboard.seo.faq.q3: How often do Today and This week reset?
game.leaderboard.seo.faq.a3: Today resets at midnight UTC. This week resets Monday 00:00 UTC. All-time never resets; it always shows the strongest saved scores.
game.leaderboard.seo.faq.q4: Can the same person appear more than once?
game.leaderboard.seo.faq.a4: Yes. Each saved run is its own score. If you post multiple strong finishes, more than one of your lines can sit on the board at once.
game.leaderboard.seo.faq.q5: Where do I play a new run?
game.leaderboard.seo.faq.a5: Open the Play tab on 73-9.org, spend the $100M bankroll across five wheel spins, and simulate. Sign in first if you want that result saved to these standings.

game.seo.title: What is the 73-9 game?
game.seo.intro: 73-9 is the number that rewrote basketball history—and the free browser challenge at 73-9.org. You get $100 million, five spins of a wheel, and one job: build a starting five that can stand up to the 2015-16 Golden State Warriors.
game.seo.how.title: Five spins. One shot at history.
game.seo.how.step1.title: Land a franchise season
game.seo.how.step1.body: The wheel stops on a random team-year anywhere from 1990 to now — that roster is your market.
game.seo.how.step2.title: Ink one contract
game.seo.how.step2.body: Take exactly one player. Pay what their deal would cost under the 2026 salary cap.
game.seo.how.step3.title: Stay under the ceiling
game.seo.how.step3.body: Repeat until you have five. Overspend early and the last seats are minimum-salary scraps.
game.seo.how.step4.title: Face the 73–9 wall
game.seo.how.step4.body: We run an 82-game season and show how often your five topples the 2015–16 Warriors — plus the best lineup you left on the table.
game.seo.what.heading: Where 73-9 comes from
game.seo.what.p1: In 2015-16 the Warriors went 73-9, edging past the 1995-96 Bulls' 72-10 for the best regular-season mark the NBA has ever recorded. This game turns that benchmark into a puzzle: you are not handed every star at once. A wheel lands on a random team-season from 1990 to today. You may sign exactly one player from that roster, and every dollar comes out of a single bankroll.
game.seo.what.p2: Five spins cover the five positions. Once the lineup locks, an 82-game simulation reports how often your squad would topple the Warriors who authored the record. Historical box scores and minutes feed the player pool; ratings and prices create the economy. Results are entertainment—not predictions. Every run reshuffles the wheel, so every bankroll puzzle is new.
game.seo.budget.heading: The $100M budget is the whole game
game.seo.budget.p1: Each player is priced by what that season's production would be worth against the 2026 salary cap. A prime Jokic or a 33-9-9 Luka can devour most of your cash in one signing. Land a megastar and the other four spots become role players, veterans, and the occasional minimum. Five max contracts would cost nearly half a billion; you have one hundred million.
game.seo.budget.p2: That tension is the point. The best players make you the best team—and instantly make you poor. Winning means hunting seasons where someone was quietly elite and underpriced, then stitching five value pieces together before the money runs out. Optional re-spins tax the same pile of cash, so every reload is a strategic choice.
game.seo.sim.heading: How the simulation decides if you win
game.seo.sim.p1: Each signed player carries a rating built from real per-game scoring, playmaking, rebounding, and shooting efficiency, weighted by minutes played. Add the five ratings and you get a team-strength number. That number drives an 82-game season sim and a head-to-head projection against the 2015-16 Warriors—a club sitting near the top 0.1% of historical team strength.
game.seo.sim.p2: A merely good five loses to that bar most nights. To win consistently you need star power five deep—which the budget is designed to make almost impossible. Almost. Kerr's everyday spine that year featured Curry, Klay, Draymond, Iguodala, and Barnes: shooting gravity, switching defense, and two-way versatility that still defines the target.
game.seo.best.heading: The best squad you could have signed
game.seo.best.p1: When the sim ends, the engine looks back at the five team-seasons you landed on and computes the strongest legal five under the same $100M cap. Identical wheel luck, perfect decisions. The gap is usually a few points per game—a star you passed on for value, or a cheaper wing that should have funded a bigger swing. Learning to read that gap is how you climb from lottery vibes to a real contender. Share the result card and challenge friends to beat your win percentage.
game.seo.why.heading: Why 73-9 still matters
game.seo.why.p1: The 2015-16 Warriors set the all-time wins record and then lost the Finals. The debate over whether that team crowns the greatest regular-season club will never fully settle. This challenge keeps the argument on a scoreboard: pull legends from thirty years of team-seasons, throw them at that historic core, and see what holds up across eighty-two games.
game.seo.why.p2: The experience is free, runs in your browser, and needs no account. Player names and stats appear for information and simulation only. This independent fan project is not affiliated with the NBA, any team, or any player. Open 73-9.org, spend the hundred million wisely, and find out whether your five has what seventy-three wins requires. Questions: support@73-9.org.
game.seo.faq.title: Frequently asked questions
game.seo.faq.a1: It is the 2015-16 Golden State Warriors' regular-season record: 73 wins and 9 losses—the best in NBA history after breaking Chicago's 72-10. The challenge asks you to build a starting five that could beat that team.
game.seo.faq.a2: Spin the wheel to a random team-season from 1990 to today, sign one player, and repeat five times—one per position—while staying under $100 million. Then simulate the season to see how often your five beats the Warriors.
game.seo.faq.q3: Why can't I sign five superstars?
game.seo.faq.a3: Each player costs what their contract would be worth against the 2026 cap based on that season's production. A single superstar can cost $80–100M, nearly the entire bankroll, so you must balance star power with value signings.
game.seo.faq.a4: Every player gets a rating from real per-game stats and minutes. Your five ratings become a team-strength number that drives an 82-game simulation and a head-to-head projection against the 2015-16 Warriors near the historical top 0.1%.
game.seo.faq.q5: What is the best squad you could have signed?
game.seo.faq.a5: After you simulate, the game recalculates the strongest legal five from the same five team-seasons under the same cap. Comparing your lineup to that optimal five is the fastest way to improve on the next run.
game.seo.faq.q6: Is it free? Do I need an account?
game.seo.faq.a6: Yes. It is completely free, runs in the browser with no sign-up, and is an independent project not affiliated with the NBA. Contact support@73-9.org if something breaks.
